Worked Example: ICE Arrests, Start to Finish

Open in VS Code

This worked example follows one real dataset through every chapter of the book, in order. You'll start with nothing but a file, and finish with a documented semantic model, a dashboard, and analyses that use filter expressions, joins, percent of total, window functions, and givens.

After every code cell there's a small 🎯 Try it challenge. It usually asks you to change one value, one time grain, or one field and run the cell again. Do them as you go. Each one takes a minute, and together they're the best practice in the book.

About the data

The data is a record of arrests made by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records were obtained through Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests and cleaned and published by the Deportation Data Project (GitHub) under a public-domain (CC0) license. The file used here is a snapshot of their arrests-latest.parquet, taken on November 4, 2026.

  • One row = one arrest record. About 896,000 rows, from October 1, 2022 to August 6, 2026.

  • That's U.S. government fiscal years 2023–2026. A fiscal year runs October 1 – September 30 and is named for the year it ends. FY2026 is incomplete in this snapshot.

  • Columns describe when and where the arrest happened, the ICE office responsible, how the arrest was made, the person's country of citizenship, approximate age, gender, criminal history category, case status, and whether they later departed (were removed) from the U.S.

⚠️ Read administrative data carefully. These are records kept by an agency for its own purposes, not a survey designed for research. Categories are ICE's own (for example, "Other Immigration Violator" means no criminal conviction or pending charge was recorded). Some records are duplicates, some fields are missing, and the definitions can change between releases. Every row is a real person's arrest. Describe what the data shows precisely, and say what it can't tell you. The Deportation Data Project's documentation explains the fields and known issues.

Part 1 · The Basics

A source from a file, or from a URL

Every analysis starts with a source. DuckDB can read a file on disk:

source: ice_raw is duckdb.table('data/ice_arrests.parquet')

DuckDB can just as easily read a file straight from the internet, including the latest version published by the Deportation Data Project. (This website was built offline from the local snapshot, so this version isn't run here.)

source: ice_live is duckdb.table(
  'https://github.com/deportationdata/ice/raw/refs/heads/main/data/arrests-latest.parquet'
)

🎯 Try it: In your notebook, add a cell with the ice_live source above and run run: ice_live -> { aggregate: rows is count() }. Does the live file have more rows than our snapshot?

How many rows? 

run: ice_raw -> {
  aggregate: arrest_records is count()
}
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "arrest_records": 896393
  }
]
SELECT 
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_records"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base

🎯 Try it: Add a second aggregate, people is count(unique_identifier). count(column) counts distinct values, so it counts people instead of rows. Why are there fewer people than arrest records?

Extending the source with dimensions and measures

Typing apprehension_state_filled_in gets old fast, and "count of rows" should have a name. Let's build a better source with renames, dimensions, and measures:

source: arrests is ice_raw extend {
  rename:
    arrest_date is apprehension_date
    state is apprehension_state_filled_in
    country is citizenship_country
    method is apprehension_method_simple

  dimension:
    age is age_at_apprehension_approximate
    is_female is gender = 'Female'

  measure:
    arrest_count is count()
    person_count is count(unique_identifier)
    avg_age is age.avg()
}
run: arrests -> {
  group_by: method
  aggregate: arrest_count, person_count, avg_age
}
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "method": "At-Large Arrest",
    "arrest_count": 408055,
    "person_count": 385529,
    "avg_age": 34.019365036575955
  },
  {
    "method": "Custodial Arrest",
    "arrest_count": 389386,
    "person_count": 359624,
    "avg_age": 35.01299481748188
  },
  {
    "method": "287(g) Program",
    "arrest_count": 53219,
    "person_count": 51720,
    "avg_age": 34.45175595182172
  },
  {
    "method": "Other",
    "arrest_count": 45733,
    "person_count": 42104,
    "avg_age": 32.07629064351781
  }
]
SELECT 
   base."apprehension_method_simple" as "method",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count",
   count(distinct base."unique_identifier") as "person_count",
   AVG((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")) as "avg_age"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 desc NULLS LAST

Part 2 · Time Truncation

arrest_date is a date. .year, .quarter, .month, and .week turn it into trends.

run: arrests -> {
  group_by: arrest_quarter is arrest_date.quarter
  aggregate: arrest_count
  order_by: arrest_quarter
}
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "arrest_quarter": "2022-10-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "arrest_count": 48512
  },
  {
    "arrest_quarter": "2023-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",

    "arrest_count": 39725

    "arrest_count": 34216
  },
  {
    "arrest_quarter": "2023-10-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "arrest_count": 29082
  },
  {
    "arrest_quarter": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "arrest_count": 28001
  },
  {
    "arrest_quarter": "2024-04-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "arrest_count": 29273
  },
  {
    "arrest_quarter": "2024-07-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "arrest_count": 27299
  },
  {
    "arrest_quarter": "2024-10-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "arrest_count": 26476
  },
  {
    "arrest_quarter": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "arrest_count": 48577
  }
]
SELECT 
   DATE_TRUNC('quarter', base."apprehension_date") as "arrest_quarter",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

🎯 Try it: Change .quarter to .month, then to .week. What changes about the story when the grain gets finer?

Fiscal years

The government counts in fiscal years (October – September). There's no .fiscal_year truncation, but a dimension can compute one. If the month is October or later, the fiscal year is next year:

source: arrests_fy is arrests extend {
  dimension: fiscal_year is year(arrest_date) + (pick 1 when month(arrest_date) >= 10 else 0)
}
run: arrests_fy -> {
  group_by: fiscal_year
  aggregate: arrest_count, person_count
  order_by: fiscal_year
}
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "fiscal_year": 2023,
    "arrest_count": 172515,
    "person_count": 166609
  },
  {
    "fiscal_year": 2024,
    "arrest_count": 113655,
    "person_count": 108743
  },
  {
    "fiscal_year": 2025,
    "arrest_count": 234679,
    "person_count": 221952
  },
  {
    "fiscal_year": 2026,
    "arrest_count": 375544,
    "person_count": 349713
  }
]
SELECT 
   EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) as "fiscal_year",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count",
   count(distinct base."unique_identifier") as "person_count"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

Remember that FY2026 stops on August 6, 2026, so it's missing almost two months.

🎯 Try it: Change fiscal_year to calendar_year is arrest_date.year. Why do the totals differ from the fiscal-year totals?

Extraction: which day of the week? 

run: arrests_fy -> {
  group_by: weekday is day_of_week(arrest_date)
  aggregate: arrest_count
  order_by: weekday
}
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "weekday": 1,
    "arrest_count": 57506
  },
  {
    "weekday": 2,
    "arrest_count": 133479
  },
  {

    "weekday": 7,

SELECT 
   (EXTRACT(dow FROM base."apprehension_date")+1) as "weekday",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

(1 = Sunday, 7 = Saturday.)

🎯 Try it: Change day_of_week(arrest_date) to month(arrest_date). Are some months of the year consistently busier?

Time between two dates

How long between an arrest and a recorded departure from the U.S.?

run: arrests_fy -> {
  where: departed_date is not null
  group_by: fiscal_year
  aggregate: avg_days_to_departure is avg(days(arrest_date to departed_date))
  order_by: fiscal_year
}
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "fiscal_year": 2023,
    "avg_days_to_departure": 170.0817374224365
  },
  {
    "fiscal_year": 2024,
    "avg_days_to_departure": 105.84319674175048
  },
  {
    "fiscal_year": 2025,
    "avg_days_to_departure": 56.478326897659834
  },
  {
    "fiscal_year": 2026,
    "avg_days_to_departure": 27.733092382015904
  }
]
SELECT 
   EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) as "fiscal_year",
   AVG(DATE_SUB('day', base."apprehension_date", base."departed_date")) as "avg_days_to_departure"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
WHERE base."departed_date" IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

Careful: recent arrests haven't had as much time for a departure to happen, so later years are cut short.

🎯 Try it: Change days(...) to months(...), and avg to max.

Part 3 · Views and Nesting

Let's save the most useful queries as views, and add a couple of tidier dimensions:

source: arrests_v is arrests_fy extend {
  dimension:
    criminality is regexp_replace!string(apprehension_criminality, r'^[0-9] ', '')
    aor is replace(apprehension_aor, ' Area of Responsibility', '')

  view: by_month is {
    group_by: arrest_month is arrest_date.month
    aggregate: arrest_count
    order_by: arrest_month
  }
  view: by_country is {
    group_by: country
    aggregate: arrest_count
    limit: 10
  }
  view: by_criminality is {
    group_by: criminality
    aggregate: arrest_count
  }
}
run: arrests_v -> by_country

WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT
    group_set,
    REPLACE(base."apprehension_aor",' Area of Responsibility','') as "aor__0",
    CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__0",
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      base."citizenship_country"
      END as "country__1",
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__1"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT UNNEST(GENERATE_SERIES(0,1,1)) as group_set  ) as group_set
  GROUP BY 1,2,4
)
, __stage1 AS (
  SELECT
    *,
   CASE WHEN GROUP_SET=0 THEN
                 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY group_set ORDER BY  "arrest_count__0" desc) END  as __row_number__0,
  CASE WHEN GROUP_SET=1 THEN
                 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CAST("aor__0" as VARCHAR), group_set ORDER BY  "arrest_count__1" desc) END  as __row_number__1 
  FROM __stage0
)
, __stage2 AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    MAX(CASE WHEN group_set IN (0,1) THEN CASE WHEN (GROUP_SET = 0 AND __row_number__0 > 8) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
                 END) OVER(PARTITION BY CAST("aor__0" as VARCHAR)) as __shaving__0 
  FROM __stage1 WHERE  NOT ((GROUP_SET = 1 AND __row_number__1 > 5))
)
, __stage3 AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM __stage2
  WHERE NOT ((group_set IN (0,1) AND __shaving__0 > 0)
  )
)
SELECT
  "aor__0" as "aor",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN "arrest_count__0" END) as "arrest_count",
  COALESCE(LIST({
    "country": "country__1", 
    "arrest_count": "arrest_count__1"}  ORDER BY  "arrest_count__1" DESC NULLS LAST) FILTER (WHERE group_set=1),[]) as "top_countries"
FROM __stage3
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 desc NULLS LAST
LIMIT 8

WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT
    group_set,
    EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) as "fiscal_year__0",
    CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__0",
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      regexp_replace(base."apprehension_criminality",'^[0-9] ','')
      END as "criminality__1",
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__1",
    CASE WHEN group_set IN (2,3) THEN
      base."apprehension_method_simple"
      END as "method__2",
    CASE WHEN group_set=2 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__2",
    CASE WHEN group_set=3 THEN
      base."apprehension_state_filled_in"
      END as "state__3",
    CASE WHEN group_set=3 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__3"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT UNNEST(GENERATE_SERIES(0,3,1)) as group_set  ) as group_set
  GROUP BY 1,2,4,6,8
)
, __stage1 AS (
  SELECT
    *,
   CASE WHEN GROUP_SET=3 THEN
                 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CAST("method__2" as VARCHAR),CAST("fiscal_year__0" as VARCHAR), group_set ORDER BY  "arrest_count__3" desc) END  as __row_number__3 
  FROM __stage0
)
, __stage2 AS (
  SELECT * FROM __stage1
   WHERE  NOT ((GROUP_SET = 3 AND __row_number__3 > 3))
)
, __stage3 AS (
  SELECT 
    CASE WHEN group_set=3 THEN 2 ELSE group_set END as group_set,
    "fiscal_year__0" as "fiscal_year__0",
    FIRST("arrest_count__0") FILTER (WHERE "arrest_count__0" IS NOT NULL) as "arrest_count__0",
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      "criminality__1"
      END as "criminality__1",
    FIRST("arrest_count__1") FILTER (WHERE "arrest_count__1" IS NOT NULL) as "arrest_count__1",
    CASE WHEN group_set IN (2,3) THEN
      "method__2"
      END as "method__2",
    FIRST("arrest_count__2") FILTER (WHERE "arrest_count__2" IS NOT NULL) as "arrest_count__2",
    COALESCE(LIST({
      "state": "state__3", 
      "arrest_count": "arrest_count__3"}  ORDER BY  "arrest_count__3" DESC NULLS LAST) FILTER (WHERE group_set=3),[]) as "top_states__2"
  FROM __stage2
  GROUP BY 1,2,4,6
)
SELECT
  "fiscal_year__0" as "fiscal_year",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN "arrest_count__0" END) as "arrest_count",
  COALESCE(LIST({
    "criminality": "criminality__1", 
    "arrest_count": "arrest_count__1"}  ORDER BY  "arrest_count__1" DESC NULLS LAST) FILTER (WHERE group_set=1),[]) as "by_criminality",
  COALESCE(LIST({
    "method": "method__2", 
    "arrest_count": "arrest_count__2", 
    "top_states": "top_states__2"}  ORDER BY  "arrest_count__2" DESC NULLS LAST) FILTER (WHERE group_set=2),[]) as "by_method"
FROM __stage3
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

SELECT 
   DATE_TRUNC('month', base."apprehension_date") as "arrest_month",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count",
   regexp_replace(base."apprehension_criminality",'^[0-9] ','') as "criminality"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
GROUP BY 1,3
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

SELECT 
   EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) as "fiscal_year",
   base."apprehension_method_simple" as "method",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

🎯 Try it: Remove .stack to put the bars side by side. Which version makes it easier to compare methods?

KPIs and formats 

# big_value
run: arrests_v -> {
  where: fiscal_year = 2025
  aggregate:
    # label="Arrests, FY2025"
    arrest_count
    # label="People"
    person_count
    # label="Convicted criminal"
    # percent
    pct_convicted is count() { where: criminality = 'Convicted Criminal' } / count()
    # label="Average age"
    # number="0.0"
    avg_age
}
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "arrest_count": 234679,
    "person_count": 221952,
    "pct_convicted": 0.40403274259733507,
    "avg_age": 35.036909991946445
  }
]
SELECT 
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count",
   count(distinct base."unique_identifier") as "person_count",
   (COUNT(CASE WHEN (regexp_replace(base."apprehension_criminality",'^[0-9] ',''))='Convicted Criminal' THEN 1 END))*1.0/COUNT(1) as "pct_convicted",
   AVG((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")) as "avg_age"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
WHERE (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2025

    ],

WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT
    group_set,
    CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__0",
    CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN
      count(distinct base."unique_identifier")
      END as "person_count__0",
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      DATE_TRUNC('month', base."apprehension_date")
      END as "arrest_month__1",
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__1",
    CASE WHEN group_set=2 THEN
      regexp_replace(base."apprehension_criminality",'^[0-9] ','')
      END as "criminality__2",
    CASE WHEN group_set=2 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__2",
    CASE WHEN group_set=3 THEN
      base."citizenship_country"
      END as "country__3",
    CASE WHEN group_set=3 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__3"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT UNNEST(GENERATE_SERIES(0,3,1)) as group_set  ) as group_set
  WHERE (REPLACE(base."apprehension_aor",' Area of Responsibility',''))='Chicago'
  GROUP BY 1,4,6,8
)
, __stage1 AS (
  SELECT
    *,
   CASE WHEN GROUP_SET=3 THEN
                 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY group_set ORDER BY  "arrest_count__3" desc) END  as __row_number__3 
  FROM __stage0
)
, __stage2 AS (
  SELECT * FROM __stage1
   WHERE  NOT ((GROUP_SET = 3 AND __row_number__3 > 5))
)
SELECT
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN "arrest_count__0" END) as "arrest_count",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN "person_count__0" END) as "person_count",
  COALESCE(LIST({
    "arrest_month": "arrest_month__1", 
    "arrest_count": "arrest_count__1"}  ORDER BY  "arrest_month__1" ASC NULLS LAST) FILTER (WHERE group_set=1),[]) as "by_month",
  COALESCE(LIST({
    "criminality": "criminality__2", 
    "arrest_count": "arrest_count__2"}  ORDER BY  "arrest_count__2" DESC NULLS LAST) FILTER (WHERE group_set=2),[]) as "by_criminality",
  COALESCE(LIST({
    "country": "country__3", 
    "arrest_count": "arrest_count__3"}  ORDER BY  "arrest_count__3" DESC NULLS LAST) FILTER (WHERE group_set=3),[]) as "by_country"
FROM __stage2

Part 5 · Malloy Files vs. Notebooks

Everything so far lives in this notebook. That's fine for exploring, but the definitions (fiscal year, criminality, views) belong in a model file that every notebook can share. This worked example comes with that file: ice.malloy, the finished version of everything this notebook builds, documented with #" descriptions.

A selective import brings in just the source we ask for:

import { ice_arrests } from "ice.malloy"
run: ice_arrests -> by_fiscal_year
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "fiscal_year": 2023,
    "arrest_count": 171316,
    "person_count": 166609,
    "pct_convicted": 0.3078813420813001
  },
  {
    "fiscal_year": 2024,
    "arrest_count": 112572,
    "person_count": 108743,
    "pct_convicted": 0.5043971858010873
  },
  {
    "fiscal_year": 2025,
    "arrest_count": 231165,
    "person_count": 221951,
    "pct_convicted": 0.4046979430277075
  },
  {
    "fiscal_year": 2026,
    "arrest_count": 371316,
    "person_count": 349711,
    "pct_convicted": 0.27725710715401436
  }
]
SELECT 
   EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) as "fiscal_year",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count",
   count(distinct base."unique_identifier") as "person_count",
   ((COUNT(CASE WHEN (regexp_replace(base."apprehension_criminality",'^[0-9] ',''))='Convicted Criminal' THEN 1 END)))*1.0/(COUNT(1)) as "pct_convicted"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
WHERE base."duplicate_drop_row"=false
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

One line, and the whole fiscal-year report runs from the model's definitions. We'll keep building the pieces here in the notebook, so you can see each step. In Part 14 we'll come back to ice.malloy and review it.

WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT
    group_set,
    CASE WHEN group_set IN (1,2) THEN
      EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))
      END as "fiscal_year__1",
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__1",
    ((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (regexp_replace(base."apprehension_criminality",'^[0-9] ',''))='Convicted Criminal' THEN 1 END)
      END))*1.0/(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END) as "pct_convicted__1",
    CASE WHEN group_set=2 THEN
      base."citizenship_country"
      END as "country__2",
    CASE WHEN group_set=2 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__2",
    (CASE WHEN group_set=2 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)*1.0/MAX((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)) OVER (PARTITION BY CASE WHEN group_set IN (1,2) THEN
      EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))
      END) as "share_of_arrests__2"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT UNNEST(GENERATE_SERIES(0,2,1)) as group_set  ) as group_set
  WHERE (base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)
  AND ((group_set NOT IN (2) OR (group_set IN (2) AND base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)))
  GROUP BY 1,2,5
)
, __stage1 AS (
  SELECT
    *,
   CASE WHEN GROUP_SET=2 THEN
                 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CAST("fiscal_year__1" as VARCHAR), group_set ORDER BY  "arrest_count__2" desc) END  as __row_number__2 
  FROM __stage0
)
, __stage2 AS (
  SELECT * FROM __stage1
   WHERE  NOT ((GROUP_SET = 2 AND __row_number__2 > 10))
)
SELECT
  "fiscal_year__1" as "fiscal_year",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "arrest_count__1" END) as "arrest_count",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "pct_convicted__1" END) as "pct_convicted",
  COALESCE(LIST({
    "country": "country__2", 
    "arrest_count": "arrest_count__2", 
    "share_of_arrests": "share_of_arrests__2"}  ORDER BY  "arrest_count__2" DESC NULLS LAST) FILTER (WHERE group_set=2),[]) as "by_country"
FROM __stage2
WHERE group_set NOT IN (0)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

Part 7 · CSV and Parquet

Our file is Parquet. What's inside?

run: duckdb.sql("""
  SELECT * FROM parquet_metadata('data/ice_arrests.parquet')
""") -> {
  group_by: column_name is path_in_schema, compression
  aggregate:
    row_groups is count()
    # number="#,##0"
    compressed_bytes is total_compressed_size.sum()
    # number="#,##0"
    uncompressed_bytes is total_uncompressed_size.sum()
  order_by: compressed_bytes desc
  limit: 12
}
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "column_name": "unique_identifier",
    "compression": "ZSTD",
    "row_groups": 1,
    "compressed_bytes": "15143893",
    "uncompressed_bytes": "38540488"
  },
  {
    "column_name": "apprehension_date_time",
    "compression": "ZSTD",
    "row_groups": 1,
    "compressed_bytes": "5148797",
    "uncompressed_bytes": "7340356"
  },
  {
    "column_name": "row_original",
    "compression": "ZSTD",
    "row_groups": 1,
    "compressed_bytes": "1998875",
    "uncompressed_bytes": "3520305"
  },
  {
    "column_name": "apprehension_city_original",
    "compression": "ZSTD",
    "row_groups": 1,
    "compressed_bytes": "1446559",
    "uncompressed_bytes": "1771533"
  },
  {
    "column_name": "apprehension_city_common_case",
    "compression": "ZSTD",
    "row_groups": 1,
    "compressed_bytes": "1327532",
    "uncompressed_bytes": "1611117"
  },
  {
    "column_name": "apprehension_date",
    "compression": "ZSTD",
    "row_groups": 1,
    "compressed_bytes": "1217950",
    "uncompressed_bytes": "1221460"
  },
  {
    "column_name": "event_landmark",
    "compression": "ZSTD",
    "row_groups": 1,
    "compressed_bytes": "1200338",
    "uncompressed_bytes": "1466417"
  },
  {
    "column_name": "final_order_date",
    "compression": "ZSTD",
    "row_groups": 1,
    "compressed_bytes": "990346",
    "uncompressed_bytes": "1027441"
  },
  {
    "column_name": "departed_date",
    "compression": "ZSTD",
    "row_groups": 1,
    "compressed_bytes": "911906",
    "uncompressed_bytes": "915983"
  },
  {
    "column_name": "birth_year",
    "compression": "ZSTD",
    "row_groups": 1,
    "compressed_bytes": "749301",
    "uncompressed_bytes": "787991"
  }
]
SELECT 
   base."path_in_schema" as "column_name",
   base."compression" as "compression",
   COUNT(1) as "row_groups",
   COALESCE(SUM(base."total_compressed_size"),0) as "compressed_bytes",
   COALESCE(SUM(base."total_uncompressed_size"),0) as "uncompressed_bytes"
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM parquet_metadata('data/ice_arrests.parquet')
) as base
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 4 desc NULLS LAST
LIMIT 12

Three things to notice:

  • The file uses Zstd compression.

  • It's written as one row group holding all ~896,000 rows. That's fine for a file this size, but it means DuckDB can't use row-group min/max statistics to skip parts of the file. Writing it with smaller row groups, sorted by date, would let date filters skip most of the file.

  • Columns with long, repetitive text (like file_original, which says which spreadsheet each row came from) compress extremely well.

To see what CSV would cost, export it with DuckDB, in Python or the DuckDB CLI:

import duckdb, os
duckdb.sql("COPY (FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet') TO 'ice_arrests.csv' (HEADER)")
print(os.path.getsize("data/ice_arrests.parquet"), os.path.getsize("ice_arrests.csv"))

# Re-write the Parquet file sorted by date, in smaller row groups
duckdb.sql("""
  COPY (FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' ORDER BY apprehension_date)
  TO 'ice_sorted.parquet' (FORMAT parquet, COMPRESSION zstd, ROW_GROUP_SIZE 100000)
""")

🎯 Try it: Change order_by: compressed_bytes desc to order_by: uncompressed_bytes desc. Which column shrinks the most? Then run the Python above and compare the CSV's size with the Parquet file's.

Filter expressions on numbers

Arrests of young adults. Square brackets include the endpoints:

Filter expressions on dates 

run: arrests_v -> {
  aggregate:
    all_records is arrest_count
    calendar_2025 is arrest_count { where: arrest_date ~ f'2025' }
    q1_2025 is arrest_count { where: arrest_date ~ f'2025-Q1' }
    june_2025 is arrest_count { where: arrest_date ~ f'2025-06' }
    since_jan_20_2025 is arrest_count { where: arrest_date ~ f'starting 2025-01-20' }
    last_6_months is arrest_count { where: arrest_date ~ f'last 6 months' }
}
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "all_records": 896393,
    "calendar_2025": 320979,
    "q1_2025": 48577,
    "june_2025": 30436,
    "since_jan_20_2025": 578933,
    "last_6_months": 132546
  }
]
SELECT 
   (COUNT(1)) as "all_records",
   (COUNT(CASE WHEN base."apprehension_date" >= CAST(TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AS DATE) AND base."apprehension_date" < CAST(TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' AS DATE) THEN 1 END)) as "calendar_2025",
   (COUNT(CASE WHEN base."apprehension_date" >= CAST(TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AS DATE) AND base."apprehension_date" < CAST(TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01 00:00:00' AS DATE) THEN 1 END)) as "q1_2025",
   (COUNT(CASE WHEN base."apprehension_date" >= CAST(TIMESTAMP '2025-06-01 00:00:00' AS DATE) AND base."apprehension_date" < CAST(TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01 00:00:00' AS DATE) THEN 1 END)) as "june_2025",
   (COUNT(CASE WHEN base."apprehension_date" >= CAST(TIMESTAMP '2025-01-20 00:00:00' AS DATE) THEN 1 END)) as "since_jan_20_2025",
   (COUNT(CASE WHEN base."apprehension_date" >= CAST((DATE_TRUNC('month', LOCALTIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL (6) month) AS DATE) AND base."apprehension_date" < CAST(DATE_TRUNC('month', LOCALTIMESTAMP) AS DATE) THEN 1 END)) as "last_6_months"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base

last 6 months is measured from today, the moment the query runs. This snapshot ends in August 2026, so as time passes, that column will shrink to zero.

Fiscal year over fiscal year

Compare FY2024 with FY2025 for each state, using filtered measures:

run: arrests_v -> {
  extend: {
    measure:
      fy2024 is arrest_count { where: fiscal_year = 2024 }
      fy2025 is arrest_count { where: fiscal_year = 2025 }
  }
  group_by: state
  aggregate:
    fy2024
    fy2025
    # number="0.00"
    ratio is fy2025 / nullif(fy2024, 0)
  having: fy2024 > 1000
  order_by: ratio desc
  limit: 10
}

SELECT 
   base."apprehension_state_filled_in" as "state",
   (COUNT(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2024 THEN 1 END)) as "fy2024",
   (COUNT(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2025 THEN 1 END)) as "fy2025",
   ((COUNT(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2025 THEN 1 END)))*1.0/(NULLIF(((COUNT(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2024 THEN 1 END))),0)) as "ratio"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
GROUP BY 1
HAVING ((COUNT(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2024 THEN 1 END)))>1000
ORDER BY 4 desc NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

Comparing like with like

FY2026 is incomplete, so comparing it with all of FY2025 isn't fair. Compare the same stretch of each fiscal year instead: October 1 through August 6. Date ranges in filter expressions don't use brackets. A to B includes A and stops just before B, so "through August 6" is written to ...-08-07.

run: arrests_v -> {
  group_by: criminality
  aggregate:
    fy2025_to_aug6 is arrest_count { where: arrest_date ~ f'2024-10-01 to 2025-08-07' }
    fy2026_to_aug6 is arrest_count { where: arrest_date ~ f'2025-10-01 to 2026-08-07' }
    # percent
    change is arrest_count { where: arrest_date ~ f'2025-10-01 to 2026-08-07' }
      / arrest_count { where: arrest_date ~ f'2024-10-01 to 2025-08-07' } - 1
}
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "criminality": "Convicted Criminal",
    "fy2025_to_aug6": 76860,
    "fy2026_to_aug6": 104168,
    "change": 0.355295342180588
  },
  {
    "criminality": "Pending Criminal Charges",
    "fy2025_to_aug6": 54322,
    "fy2026_to_aug6": 107869,
    "change": 0.9857332204263467
  },
  {
    "criminality": "Other Immigration Violator",
    "fy2025_to_aug6": 47503,
    "fy2026_to_aug6": 163507,
    "change": 2.4420352398795866
  }
]
SELECT 
   regexp_replace(base."apprehension_criminality",'^[0-9] ','') as "criminality",
   (COUNT(CASE WHEN base."apprehension_date" >= CAST(TIMESTAMP '2024-10-01 00:00:00' AS DATE) AND base."apprehension_date" < CAST(TIMESTAMP '2025-08-07 00:00:00' AS DATE) THEN 1 END)) as "fy2025_to_aug6",
   (COUNT(CASE WHEN base."apprehension_date" >= CAST(TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01 00:00:00' AS DATE) AND base."apprehension_date" < CAST(TIMESTAMP '2026-08-07 00:00:00' AS DATE) THEN 1 END)) as "fy2026_to_aug6",
   (((COUNT(CASE WHEN base."apprehension_date" >= CAST(TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01 00:00:00' AS DATE) AND base."apprehension_date" < CAST(TIMESTAMP '2026-08-07 00:00:00' AS DATE) THEN 1 END)))*1.0/((COUNT(CASE WHEN base."apprehension_date" >= CAST(TIMESTAMP '2024-10-01 00:00:00' AS DATE) AND base."apprehension_date" < CAST(TIMESTAMP '2025-08-07 00:00:00' AS DATE) THEN 1 END))))-1 as "change"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 desc NULLS LAST

A clean source

Put the fixes into one source: drop flagged duplicates, normalize the city, turn 'NA' into a real null, and null out impossible ages:

source: arrests_clean is arrests_v extend {
  where: duplicate_drop_row = false

  dimension:
    city is upper(trim(apprehension_city_original))
    threat_level is nullif(case_threat_level, 'NA')
    age_clean is pick null when age < 1 or age > 100 else age
    age_group is age_clean ?
      pick 'Under 18' when < 18
      pick '18–24' when < 25
      pick '25–34' when < 35
      pick '35–44' when < 45
      pick '45–54' when < 55
      pick '55+' when >= 55
      else null

  measure:
    # number="0.0"
    avg_age_clean is age_clean.avg()
}
run: arrests_clean -> {
  group_by: age_group
  aggregate: arrest_count, avg_age_clean
  order_by: age_group
}
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "age_group": "18–24",
    "arrest_count": 131019,
    "avg_age_clean": 21.72768835054458
  },
  {
    "age_group": "25–34",
    "arrest_count": 312467,
    "avg_age_clean": 29.51756825520775
  },
  {
    "age_group": "35–44",
    "arrest_count": 245256,
    "avg_age_clean": 39.121452686172816
  },
  {
    "age_group": "45–54",
    "arrest_count": 121956,
    "avg_age_clean": 48.70104791892158
  },
  {
    "age_group": "55+",
    "arrest_count": 42285,
    "avg_age_clean": 59.99243230459974
  },
  {
    "age_group": "Under 18",
    "arrest_count": 33222,
    "avg_age_clean": 9.512913129853711
  },
  {
    "age_group": null,
    "arrest_count": 164,
    "avg_age_clean": null
  }
]
SELECT 
   CASE WHEN ((CASE WHEN (((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")<1) or ((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")>100)) THEN NULL ELSE (base."age_at_apprehension_approximate") END)<18) THEN 'Under 18' WHEN ((CASE WHEN (((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")<1) or ((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")>100)) THEN NULL ELSE (base."age_at_apprehension_approximate") END)<25) THEN '18–24' WHEN ((CASE WHEN (((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")<1) or ((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")>100)) THEN NULL ELSE (base."age_at_apprehension_approximate") END)<35) THEN '25–34' WHEN ((CASE WHEN (((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")<1) or ((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")>100)) THEN NULL ELSE (base."age_at_apprehension_approximate") END)<45) THEN '35–44' WHEN ((CASE WHEN (((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")<1) or ((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")>100)) THEN NULL ELSE (base."age_at_apprehension_approximate") END)<55) THEN '45–54' WHEN ((CASE WHEN (((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")<1) or ((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")>100)) THEN NULL ELSE (base."age_at_apprehension_approximate") END)>=55) THEN '55+' ELSE NULL END as "age_group",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count",
   AVG((CASE WHEN (((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")<1) or ((base."age_at_apprehension_approximate")>100)) THEN NULL ELSE (base."age_at_apprehension_approximate") END)) as "avg_age_clean"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
WHERE base."duplicate_drop_row"=false
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

Part 10 · Joins and Symmetric Aggregates

Joining a lookup table

state_regions.csv (from Chapter 14) has one row per U.S. state with its 2-letter code and Census region. The arrest data uses capitalized full names, so we join on an expression:

source: state_regions is duckdb.table('data/state_regions.csv') extend {
  primary_key: state_code
  dimension: state_upper is upper(state_name)
  measure: state_count is count()
}

source: arrests_joined is arrests_clean extend {
  join_one: state_regions on state = state_regions.state_upper
}
run: arrests_joined -> {
  group_by: state_regions.region
  aggregate: arrest_count, state_regions.state_count
}
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "region": "South",
    "arrest_count": 486398,
    "state_count": 17
  },
  {
    "region": "West",
    "arrest_count": 159600,
    "state_count": 13
  },
  {
    "region": "Northeast",
    "arrest_count": 111353,
    "state_count": 9
  },
  {
    "region": "Midwest",
    "arrest_count": 82859,
    "state_count": 12
  },
  {
    "region": null,
    "arrest_count": 46159,
    "state_count": 0
  }
]
SELECT 
   state_regions_0."region" as "region",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count",
   COUNT(DISTINCT state_regions_0."state_code") as "state_count"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
 LEFT JOIN 'data/state_regions.csv' AS state_regions_0
  ON base."apprehension_state_filled_in"=(UPPER(state_regions_0."state_name"))
WHERE base."duplicate_drop_row"=false
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 desc NULLS LAST

The null region collects the territories, military regions, and missing states, which have no match in the lookup table. state_regions.state_count counts states, not arrests, even though each state matched thousands of arrest rows. That's symmetric aggregation at work.

SELECT 
   state_regions_0."state_code" as "state_code",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
 LEFT JOIN 'data/state_regions.csv' AS state_regions_0
  ON base."apprehension_state_filled_in"=(UPPER(state_regions_0."state_name"))
WHERE ((EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2025)
AND (base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)
GROUP BY 1

One row per person: joining to a query

Some people appear in more than one arrest record. Build a person-level source with a query, give it a primary key, and join it back:

source: people is arrests_clean -> {
  where: unique_identifier is not null
  group_by: unique_identifier
  aggregate:
    arrests_of_person is count()
    first_arrest is min(arrest_date)
} extend {
  primary_key: unique_identifier
  dimension: repeat_person is arrests_of_person > 1
  measure: people_count is count()
}

source: arrests_people is arrests_joined extend {
  join_one: people with unique_identifier
}
run: arrests_people -> {
  group_by: people.repeat_person
  aggregate:
    arrest_count
    people.people_count
    # number="0.000"
    avg_arrests_per_person is people.arrests_of_person.avg()
    # number="0.000"
    avg_arrests_per_record is source.avg(people.arrests_of_person)
}
QUERY RESULTS 
[
  {
    "repeat_person": false,
    "arrest_count": 763315,
    "people_count": 763315,
    "avg_arrests_per_person": 1,
    "avg_arrests_per_record": 1
  },
  {
    "repeat_person": true,
    "arrest_count": 103335,
    "people_count": 49508,
    "avg_arrests_per_person": 2.0872384261129513,
    "avg_arrests_per_record": 2.136846179900324
  },
  {
    "repeat_person": null,
    "arrest_count": 19719,
    "people_count": 0,
    "avg_arrests_per_person": null,
    "avg_arrests_per_record": null
  }
]
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     base."unique_identifier" as "unique_identifier",
     COUNT(1) as "arrests_of_person",
     min(base."apprehension_date") as "first_arrest"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  WHERE (base."unique_identifier" IS NOT NULL)
  AND (base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT 
   people_0."arrests_of_person">1 as "repeat_person",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count",
   COUNT(DISTINCT people_0."unique_identifier") as "people_count",
   (
        SELECT AVG(a.val) as value
        FROM (
          SELECT UNNEST(list(distinct {key:people_0."unique_identifier", val: people_0."arrests_of_person"})) a
        )
      ) as "avg_arrests_per_person",
   AVG(people_0."arrests_of_person") as "avg_arrests_per_record"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
 LEFT JOIN __stage0 AS people_0
  ON people_0."unique_identifier"=base."unique_identifier"
WHERE base."duplicate_drop_row"=false
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 desc NULLS LAST

Look at the true row. people.arrests_of_person.avg() averages over people: each person counts once. source.avg(people.arrests_of_person) averages over arrest records, so someone arrested three times counts three times. Both are legitimate questions with different answers, and Malloy makes you choose which one you mean. (The null row holds the records with no person identifier, so they can't be matched to a person.)

WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT
    group_set,
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      base."citizenship_country"
      END as "country__1",
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__1",
    (CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)*1.0/MAX((CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)) OVER () as "share__1"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT UNNEST(GENERATE_SERIES(0,1,1)) as group_set  ) as group_set
  WHERE base."duplicate_drop_row"=false
  GROUP BY 1,2
)
, __stage1 AS (
  SELECT
    *,
   CASE WHEN GROUP_SET=1 THEN
                 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY group_set ORDER BY  "arrest_count__1" desc) END  as __row_number__1 
  FROM __stage0
)
, __stage2 AS (
  SELECT * FROM __stage1
   WHERE  NOT ((GROUP_SET = 1 AND __row_number__1 > 10))
)
SELECT
  "country__1" as "country",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "arrest_count__1" END) as "arrest_count",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "share__1" END) as "share"
FROM __stage2
WHERE group_set NOT IN (0)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 desc NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT
    group_set,
    CASE WHEN group_set IN (2,1) THEN
      regexp_replace(base."apprehension_criminality",'^[0-9] ','')
      END as "criminality__2",
    CASE WHEN group_set=2 THEN
      base."apprehension_method_simple"
      END as "method__2",
    CASE WHEN group_set=2 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__2",
    (CASE WHEN group_set=2 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)*1.0/MAX((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)) OVER (PARTITION BY CASE WHEN group_set IN (2,1) THEN
      regexp_replace(base."apprehension_criminality",'^[0-9] ','')
      END) as "share_of_category__2"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT UNNEST(GENERATE_SERIES(0,2,1)) as group_set  ) as group_set
  WHERE base."duplicate_drop_row"=false
  GROUP BY 1,2,3
)
SELECT
  "criminality__2" as "criminality",
  "method__2" as "method",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=2 THEN "arrest_count__2" END) as "arrest_count",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=2 THEN "share_of_category__2" END) as "share_of_category"
FROM __stage0
WHERE group_set NOT IN (0,1)
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST,4 desc NULLS LAST

Contribution to change

WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT
    group_set,
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      REPLACE(base."apprehension_aor",' Area of Responsibility','')
      END as "aor__1",
    (CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2024 THEN 1 END)
      END) as "fy2024__1",
    (CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2025 THEN 1 END)
      END) as "fy2025__1",
    ((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2025 THEN 1 END)
      END))-((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2024 THEN 1 END)
      END)) as "change__1",
    ((((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2025 THEN 1 END)
      END))-((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2024 THEN 1 END)
      END))))*1.0/MAX(((CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2025 THEN 1 END)
      END))-((CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2024 THEN 1 END)
      END))) OVER () as "contribution_to_change__1"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT UNNEST(GENERATE_SERIES(0,1,1)) as group_set  ) as group_set
  WHERE base."duplicate_drop_row"=false
  GROUP BY 1,2
)
, __stage1 AS (
  SELECT
    *,
   CASE WHEN GROUP_SET=1 THEN
                 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY group_set ORDER BY  "contribution_to_change__1" desc) END  as __row_number__1 
  FROM __stage0
)
, __stage2 AS (
  SELECT * FROM __stage1
   WHERE  NOT ((GROUP_SET = 1 AND __row_number__1 > 10))
)
SELECT
  "aor__1" as "aor",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "fy2024__1" END) as "fy2024",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "fy2025__1" END) as "fy2025",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "change__1" END) as "change",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "contribution_to_change__1" END) as "contribution_to_change"
FROM __stage2
WHERE group_set NOT IN (0)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 5 desc NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

Index: over- or under-represented?

Compare the mix of countries in one office with the national mix, using filtered measures as in Chapter 11. An index of 200 means "twice as common here as nationally":

run: arrests_clean -> {

  aggregate:

    # number="0"

      / (arrest_count / all(arrest_count)) * 100
  having: arrest_count { where: aor = 'Miami' } > 1000
  order_by: miami_index desc

}

WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT
    group_set,
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      base."citizenship_country"
      END as "country__1",
    (CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (REPLACE(base."apprehension_aor",' Area of Responsibility',''))='Miami' THEN 1 END)
      END) as "miami_arrests__1",
    (((((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (REPLACE(base."apprehension_aor",' Area of Responsibility',''))='Miami' THEN 1 END)
      END))*1.0/MAX((CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (REPLACE(base."apprehension_aor",' Area of Responsibility',''))='Miami' THEN 1 END)
      END)) OVER ()))*1.0/(((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)*1.0/MAX((CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)) OVER ())))*100 as "miami_index__1"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT UNNEST(GENERATE_SERIES(0,1,1)) as group_set  ) as group_set
  WHERE base."duplicate_drop_row"=false
  GROUP BY 1,2
  HAVING (group_set<>1 OR (group_set=1 AND ((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
    COUNT(CASE WHEN (REPLACE(base."apprehension_aor",' Area of Responsibility',''))='Miami' THEN 1 END)
    END))>1000))
)
, __stage1 AS (
  SELECT
    *,
   CASE WHEN GROUP_SET=1 THEN
                 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY group_set ORDER BY  "miami_index__1" desc) END  as __row_number__1 
  FROM __stage0
)
, __stage2 AS (
  SELECT * FROM __stage1
   WHERE  NOT ((GROUP_SET = 1 AND __row_number__1 > 10))
)
SELECT
  "country__1" as "country",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "miami_arrests__1" END) as "miami_arrests",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "miami_index__1" END) as "miami_index"
FROM __stage2
WHERE group_set NOT IN (0)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 3 desc NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

Part 12 · Pipelines and Window Calculations

A two-stage pipeline: how often are people re-arrested?

Stage 1 counts arrests per person. Stage 2 counts people by that number:

run: arrests_clean -> {
  where: unique_identifier is not null
  group_by: unique_identifier
  aggregate: arrests_of_person is count()
} -> {
  group_by: arrests_of_person
  aggregate: people is count()
  order_by: arrests_of_person
}
QUERY RESULTS

    "people": 763315

WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     base."unique_identifier" as "unique_identifier",
     COUNT(1) as "arrests_of_person"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  WHERE (base."unique_identifier" IS NOT NULL)
  AND (base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT 
   base."arrests_of_person" as "arrests_of_person",
   COUNT(1) as "people"
FROM __stage0 as base
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

SELECT 
   DATE_TRUNC('month', base."apprehension_date") as "arrest_month",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count",
   LAG((COUNT(1))) OVER(  ORDER BY  DATE_TRUNC('month', base."apprehension_date") ASC NULLS LAST ) as "prev_month",
   ((COUNT(1))*1.0/(LAG((COUNT(1))) OVER(  ORDER BY  DATE_TRUNC('month', base."apprehension_date") ASC NULLS LAST )))-1 as "pct_change"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
WHERE (base."apprehension_date" >= CAST(TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AS DATE) AND base."apprehension_date" < CAST(TIMESTAMP '2026-08-01 00:00:00' AS DATE))
AND (base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

🎯 Try it: Change .month to .quarter, and lag(arrest_count) to lag(arrest_count, 4) for change from the same quarter a year earlier.

rank within each fiscal year 

run: arrests_clean -> {
  where: fiscal_year ~ f'[2024 to 2025]'
  group_by: fiscal_year, aor
  aggregate: arrest_count
  calculate: office_rank is rank() {
    partition_by: fiscal_year
    order_by: arrest_count desc
  }
} -> {
  where: office_rank <= 5
  select: fiscal_year, office_rank, aor, arrest_count
  order_by: fiscal_year, office_rank
}

WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) as "fiscal_year",
     REPLACE(base."apprehension_aor",' Area of Responsibility','') as "aor",
     COUNT(1) as "arrest_count",
     RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))) ORDER BY (COUNT(1)) DESC ) as "office_rank"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  WHERE ((EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))) >= 2024  AND  (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))) <= 2025)
  AND (base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)
  GROUP BY 1,2
)
SELECT 
   base."fiscal_year" as "fiscal_year",
   base."office_rank" as "office_rank",
   base."aor" as "aor",
   base."arrest_count" as "arrest_count"
FROM __stage0 as base
WHERE base."office_rank"<=5
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST,2 ASC NULLS LAST

Stage 1 ranks offices within each year (partition_by:), and stage 2 keeps the top 5. Calculations can't be filtered in the same stage, so a pipeline does it.

🎯 Try it: Change aor to state, and <= 5 to <= 3.

SELECT 
   (DATE_TRUNC('week', (base."apprehension_date" + INTERVAL '1' DAY)) - INTERVAL '1' DAY) as "arrest_week",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count",
   AVG((COUNT(1))) OVER(  ORDER BY  (DATE_TRUNC('week', (base."apprehension_date" + INTERVAL '1' DAY)) - INTERVAL '1' DAY) ASC NULLS LAST ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 0 FOLLOWING) as "four_week_avg"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
WHERE base."duplicate_drop_row"=false
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

run: arrests_clean -> {
  where: fiscal_year ~ f'[2024 to 2026]'
  group_by: fiscal_year, arrest_month is arrest_date.month
  aggregate: arrest_count
  order_by: arrest_month
  calculate: fiscal_ytd is sum_cumulative(arrest_count) {
    partition_by: fiscal_year
    order_by: arrest_month
  }
  limit: 15
}

SELECT 
   EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) as "fiscal_year",
   DATE_TRUNC('month', base."apprehension_date") as "arrest_month",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count",
   SUM((COUNT(1))) OVER(PARTITION BY (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))) ORDER BY (DATE_TRUNC('month', base."apprehension_date")) ) as "fiscal_ytd"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
WHERE ((EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))) >= 2024  AND  (EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))) <= 2026)
AND (base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 2 ASC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 15

The running total restarts every October, when a new fiscal year begins.

Part 13 · Givens

The office comparison in Part 11 typed 'Miami' four times. Givens fix that: declare the value once, use it everywhere with $.

##! experimental.givens
given:
  OFFICE :: string is 'Miami'
  COUNTRIES :: filter<string> is f'MEXICO, GUATEMALA, HONDURAS, VENEZUELA'
  SINCE :: date is @2025-01-20
run: arrests_clean -> {
  group_by: country
  aggregate:
    office_arrests is arrest_count { where: aor = $OFFICE }
    # number="0"
    office_index is (arrest_count { where: aor = $OFFICE } / all(arrest_count { where: aor = $OFFICE }))
      / (arrest_count / all(arrest_count)) * 100
  having: arrest_count { where: aor = $OFFICE } > 1000
  order_by: office_index desc
  limit: 10
}
QUERY RESULTS

  },

WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT
    group_set,
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      base."citizenship_country"
      END as "country__1",
    (CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (REPLACE(base."apprehension_aor",' Area of Responsibility',''))='Miami' THEN 1 END)
      END) as "office_arrests__1",
    (((((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (REPLACE(base."apprehension_aor",' Area of Responsibility',''))='Miami' THEN 1 END)
      END))*1.0/MAX((CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (REPLACE(base."apprehension_aor",' Area of Responsibility',''))='Miami' THEN 1 END)
      END)) OVER ()))*1.0/(((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)*1.0/MAX((CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)) OVER ())))*100 as "office_index__1"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT UNNEST(GENERATE_SERIES(0,1,1)) as group_set  ) as group_set
  WHERE base."duplicate_drop_row"=false
  GROUP BY 1,2
  HAVING (group_set<>1 OR (group_set=1 AND ((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
    COUNT(CASE WHEN (REPLACE(base."apprehension_aor",' Area of Responsibility',''))='Miami' THEN 1 END)
    END))>1000))
)
, __stage1 AS (
  SELECT
    *,
   CASE WHEN GROUP_SET=1 THEN
                 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY group_set ORDER BY  "office_index__1" desc) END  as __row_number__1 
  FROM __stage0
)
, __stage2 AS (
  SELECT * FROM __stage1
   WHERE  NOT ((GROUP_SET = 1 AND __row_number__1 > 10))
)
SELECT
  "country__1" as "country",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "office_arrests__1" END) as "office_arrests",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "office_index__1" END) as "office_index"
FROM __stage2
WHERE group_set NOT IN (0)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 3 desc NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

SELECT 
   DATE_TRUNC('month', base."apprehension_date") as "arrest_month",
   base."citizenship_country" as "country",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
WHERE (base."citizenship_country" IN ('MEXICO', 'GUATEMALA', 'HONDURAS', 'VENEZUELA'))
AND (base."apprehension_date">=DATE '2025-01-20')
AND (base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST

A filter<string> given holds a whole filter expression, which a user (or an app) could type.

WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT
    group_set,
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__1",
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      count(distinct base."unique_identifier")
      END as "person_count__1",
    ((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (regexp_replace(base."apprehension_criminality",'^[0-9] ',''))='Convicted Criminal' THEN 1 END)
      END))*1.0/(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END) as "pct_convicted__1",
    CASE WHEN group_set=2 THEN
      DATE_TRUNC('month', base."apprehension_date")
      END as "arrest_month__2",
    CASE WHEN group_set=2 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__2",
    CASE WHEN group_set=3 THEN
      regexp_replace(base."apprehension_criminality",'^[0-9] ','')
      END as "criminality__3",
    CASE WHEN group_set=3 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__3",
    CASE WHEN group_set=4 THEN
      base."citizenship_country"
      END as "country__4",
    CASE WHEN group_set=4 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__4",
    (CASE WHEN group_set=4 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)*1.0/MAX((CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)) OVER () as "share_of_arrests__4",
    CASE WHEN group_set=5 THEN
      REPLACE(base."apprehension_aor",' Area of Responsibility','')
      END as "aor__5",
    CASE WHEN group_set=5 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__5",
    ((CASE WHEN group_set=5 THEN
      COUNT(CASE WHEN (regexp_replace(base."apprehension_criminality",'^[0-9] ',''))='Convicted Criminal' THEN 1 END)
      END))*1.0/(CASE WHEN group_set=5 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END) as "pct_convicted__5"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT UNNEST(GENERATE_SERIES(0,5,1)) as group_set  ) as group_set
  WHERE ((EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2025)
  AND (base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)
  AND ((group_set NOT IN (2) OR (group_set IN (2) AND base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)))
  AND ((group_set NOT IN (3) OR (group_set IN (3) AND base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)))
  AND ((group_set NOT IN (4) OR (group_set IN (4) AND base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)))
  AND ((group_set NOT IN (5) OR (group_set IN (5) AND base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)))
  GROUP BY 1,5,7,9,12
)
, __stage1 AS (
  SELECT
    *,
   CASE WHEN GROUP_SET=4 THEN
                 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY group_set ORDER BY  "arrest_count__4" desc) END  as __row_number__4,
  CASE WHEN GROUP_SET=5 THEN
                 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY group_set ORDER BY  "arrest_count__5" desc) END  as __row_number__5 
  FROM __stage0
)
, __stage2 AS (
  SELECT * FROM __stage1
   WHERE  NOT ((GROUP_SET = 4 AND __row_number__4 > 10)
   OR (GROUP_SET = 5 AND __row_number__5 > 10))
)
SELECT
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "arrest_count__1" END) as "arrest_count",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "person_count__1" END) as "person_count",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "pct_convicted__1" END) as "pct_convicted",
  COALESCE(LIST({
    "arrest_month": "arrest_month__2", 
    "arrest_count": "arrest_count__2"}  ORDER BY  "arrest_month__2" ASC NULLS LAST) FILTER (WHERE group_set=2),[]) as "by_month",
  COALESCE(LIST({
    "criminality": "criminality__3", 
    "arrest_count": "arrest_count__3"}  ORDER BY  "arrest_count__3" DESC NULLS LAST) FILTER (WHERE group_set=3),[]) as "by_criminality",
  COALESCE(LIST({
    "country": "country__4", 
    "arrest_count": "arrest_count__4", 
    "share_of_arrests": "share_of_arrests__4"}  ORDER BY  "arrest_count__4" DESC NULLS LAST) FILTER (WHERE group_set=4),[]) as "by_country",
  COALESCE(LIST({
    "aor": "aor__5", 
    "arrest_count": "arrest_count__5", 
    "pct_convicted": "pct_convicted__5"}  ORDER BY  "arrest_count__5" DESC NULLS LAST) FILTER (WHERE group_set=5),[]) as "by_aor"
FROM __stage2
WHERE group_set NOT IN (0)

WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT
    group_set,
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      base."citizenship_country"
      END as "country__1",
    CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END as "arrest_count__1",
    (CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)*1.0/MAX((CASE WHEN group_set=0 THEN
      COUNT(1)
      END)) OVER () as "share_of_arrests__1"
  FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT UNNEST(GENERATE_SERIES(0,1,1)) as group_set  ) as group_set
  WHERE ((EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)))=2025)
  AND (base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)
  GROUP BY 1,2
)
, __stage1 AS (
  SELECT
    *,
   CASE WHEN GROUP_SET=1 THEN
                 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY group_set ORDER BY  "arrest_count__1" desc) END  as __row_number__1 
  FROM __stage0
)
, __stage2 AS (
  SELECT * FROM __stage1
   WHERE  NOT ((GROUP_SET = 1 AND __row_number__1 > 10))
)
SELECT
  "country__1" as "country",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "arrest_count__1" END) as "arrest_count",
  MAX(CASE WHEN group_set=1 THEN "share_of_arrests__1" END) as "share_of_arrests"
FROM __stage2
WHERE group_set NOT IN (0)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 desc NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

SELECT 
   EXTRACT(year FROM base."apprehension_date")+((CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(month FROM base."apprehension_date")>=10) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) as "fiscal_year",
   COUNT(1) as "arrest_count",
   count(distinct base."unique_identifier") as "person_count",
   ((COUNT(CASE WHEN (regexp_replace(base."apprehension_criminality",'^[0-9] ',''))='Convicted Criminal' THEN 1 END)))*1.0/(COUNT(1)) as "pct_convicted"
FROM 'data/ice_arrests.parquet' as base
WHERE (base."duplicate_drop_row"=false)
AND (base."apprehension_state_filled_in"='TEXAS')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST
